hook: If you replay conversations in your head for hours after they end — I want to show you what's actually happening.
topic: Post-conversation rumination as a threat-response artifact
body:
**If you replay conversations in your head for hours after they end — I want to show you what's actually happening.**

It's not that you're oversensitive. It's not that the conversation was actually that important.

It's that your nervous system flagged the interaction as a potential threat — maybe a moment of perceived judgment, a pause that felt too long, something you said that landed wrong — and it didn't finish processing it.

Unresolved threat signals don't disappear. They recirculate. Your brain keeps returning to the scene because it is genuinely trying to solve something. It's running a threat-detection loop on incomplete data.

The problem is you keep feeding it more data. Every replay gives it new material to analyse. And the loop continues.

The exit isn't to think harder about the conversation. It's to signal to your nervous system that the threat has been processed and resolved — and you do that through the body, not through more thinking.

A slow, extended exhale. Physical grounding. Something that tells the system: the scene is closed.

The full guide is in my bio — including the specific sequence for when you can't stop the loop.
